quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:

options.text: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
It is an ambulance.
It is a school bus.
The vehicle is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility drops to 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make visibility worse.

questions.question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and quickly steer back onto the road.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Take your foot off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back on by keeping both hands on the wheel and turning slightly. Check traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic or nearly the same.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted freeway speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic or nearly the same.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Check that your tires have good tread.
Check that your tires are properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct pressure. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: When should you drive in a reversible lane showing a red X signal?

options.text: When there is no oncoming traffic.
When you are passing the car in front of you.
Never.
Between sunset and sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Lane signals show which lanes are open or closed and if toll booths are open. A red X means the lane is closed. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down to safely navigate the curves.

questions.question: When following a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Follow a motorcycle with at least three to four seconds of distance. Motorcycles stop quickly, and you need extra space to avoid hitting the rider if they fall. Falls are more likely on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges.

questions.question: You see a green light ahead, but cars are blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Start to enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter the intersection until you can drive all the way across.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter the intersection until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The full lane width like other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly that they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert and safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed.
The highway ahead has construction or maintenance work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead has construction or maintenance work.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you to slow down and drive carefully because workers and equipment are ahead.

questions.question: What is a good passing rule?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases crash risk. If you pass frequently, you will keep passing others. Drive with traffic, stay at the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to:

options.text: Enter a school zone.
Yield to other traffic.
Enter a construction zone.
Cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs mean you must yield. Wait until the road is clear and safe before you go.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the leading cause of car crashes. Any distraction makes you miss signs and sounds that help you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, move to the right side of the road and stop. Let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then move to the right and stop.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows your nerves and body functions. It reduces your ability to focus and stay alert.
